questions.question: Per-test timeout: which mechanism? (The slowest test in .test_durations_pass1 takes 48 s; the next slowest is under 3 s.)

options.label: pytest-timeout (Recommended)
options.description: New dev dependency `pytest-timeout`. On Windows only its thread method exists: it dumps stacks and kills the worker, and xdist then reports that the test crashed, by name, and starts a new worker. This is the standard tool for the job.

options.label: faulthandler_timeout
options.description: Built into pytest, so no new dependency. It only dumps stack traces after N seconds. The test does not fail and the run still hangs, so this gives diagnosis but no bound.

options.label: Watchdog in run_tests.py
options.description: No new dependency. The launcher kills the whole pytest tree when no output appears for N seconds. The run is bounded, but the hung test is only named by the last progress line, which is weaker than a per-test failure.

questions.question: Where should the timeout apply, and at what value?

options.label: Local, 300 s (Recommended)
options.description: run_tests.py adds `--timeout=300` unless the caller passes its own. `RS_TEST_TIMEOUT` overrides it. CI, the mutation runs and bare pytest are unaffected, which fits 'CI out of scope'.

options.label: Everywhere, 300 s
options.description: `timeout = 300` in [tool.pytest.ini_options], so it applies to CI, mutation runs and ad-hoc pytest as well. CI behaviour changes even though no workflow file is edited.

options.label: Local, 120 s
options.description: Same as the first option but tighter: about 2.5 times the slowest test. Risk of false kills when the machine is loaded.

questions.question: When the suite lock is held, what should a second run do?

options.label: Wait ≤15 min, then fail (Recommended)
options.description: Prints the holder's PID, checkout and start time, then a progress line every 30 s. After 15 minutes it exits with a distinct code. `RS_TEST_LOCK_WAIT=<seconds>` overrides the bound, and 0 means refuse at once. This lines up with the 15-minute background deadline.

options.label: Wait without a bound
options.description: Prints the same messages but never gives up. Only the session's 15-minute deadline bounds it. A foreground call still dies at the 600 s tool limit.

options.label: Refuse immediately
options.description: Exits at once with a message naming the holder. The session has to retry itself. Simplest, but it pushes polling onto the session.

questions.question: Review finding: the 15-minute lock wait you chose doesn't fit either session bound. A foreground call is cut off at 600 s before the launcher can give up, and a background run that gets the lock late is killed by the 15-minute deadline partway through. What should the default lock wait be?

options.label: 5 min (Recommended)
options.description: Default RS_TEST_LOCK_WAIT=300. A foreground run can wait 300 s and still have about 300 s to run inside the 600 s limit (the gate's test step took 164 s here). A background run waits at most 5 min, which leaves about 10 min of its 15-minute deadline for the run.

options.label: 8 min
options.description: Default 480 s. Waits longer for a busy machine, but a foreground run that gets the lock late has only about 120 s left, less than one test step.

options.label: Keep 15 min
options.description: Leave the default at 900 s. Reply to the finding that the session's deadline, not the launcher, is the bound. Exit 75 then rarely fires in practice.

questions.question: Which follow-ups should become backlog items in this PR? Note: UNDERSTANDING.md says this plan mints no new backlog IDs, and parallel sessions should mint only reserved IDs (next safe on this tree: BUG-315, BK-421). Choosing any option overrides that rule for these items.

options.label: BUG: moto port race (Recommended)
options.description: tests/conftest.py:80/177: `_free_port()` closes the socket and then `ThreadedMotoServer(port=...)` binds 0.0.0.0 with SO_REUSEADDR. Two servers can silently share a port (cross-run S3 state), or a failed bind makes `start()` wait forever. That is a candidate cause of the 97% idle stall. No item exists (searched `backlog-find moto`). Fix: about three lines, test-first. It needs its own PR.

options.label: BK: CI jobs have no timeout
options.description: There are zero `timeout-minutes` in .github/workflows (searched), so a hung test in CI runs to GitHub's 6 h job default. BK-419 bounds hangs only locally. Options are a job `timeout-minutes` or `--timeout` in CI's inline pytest. infra.ci, out of BK-419's scope.

options.label: BK: lock frees on launcher kill
options.description: If the launcher is killed (TaskStop) while its pytest children survive, the lock frees while they still run. Fix: have pytest hold the lock (plugin/conftest), or kill the child tree when the launcher dies. This is the remaining gap in BK-419's guarantee.

options.label: BK: measure 4 vs 8 workers
options.description: Time test-cov-s1 at RS_TEST_WORKERS=4 and at 8 on an idle machine, then keep the faster. The change to 4 rests on an audit measured on a 4-core container. It is a measurement, so it may fit better as a note than an item.
